clue.text: Back among top celebrities, article names record-holder

indicators.note: among places the turned-round letters inside the phrase for the top celebrities

parts.note: the A-list is the group of the most famous stars

indicators.note: back tells you the article and the names together are read from right to left

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
N is an abbreviation for name, so names in the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A returning star, once more in elite company, is credited in a piece with holding a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The record-holder keeps written chronicles, not sporting records. 'Back' turns the article and the two names round together to NNA before 'among' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a chronicler who writes yearly histories literally keeps records.

clue.text: Occasion for penny to drop mark sign, suitably attired for wedding?

indicators.note: being attired in something means wearing it, so the other letters go inside the garment

parts.note: a hat is the traditional thing to wear to a wedding, the question mark admitting it is only an example
M is the abbreviation for the old German currency, the mark
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A coin falls at a wedding, leaving a mark or sign on a smartly dressed guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suitably attired for wedding?' means wearing A HAT, so M and OMEN sit inside A HAT. In British idiom 'the penny drops' when someone finally understands.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the instant when understanding suddenly arrives is when the penny drops.

clue.text: Most missing art teacher, at first, after church body's absorbed one

indicators.note: after places the teacher's letter behind the church part of the answer
absorbed says the church word has taken the single letter inside itself

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church; with the possessive s it gives NAVES
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A congregation that has taken in a new member is the group pining hardest for its art teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' here means cunning, so the one most lacking it is the most innocent. 'absorbed' puts I inside NAVES, and 'at first ... after' adds T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: someone with the least guile or cunning is the most artless.

clue.text: Tips exchanged by tinker and sailor

indicators.note: exchanged says the first and last letters of the word trade places with each other
the tips of a word are its first and last letters, the two that change position

parts.note: in British use a tinker is a mischievous child, a rascal

explanation.surface: A travelling mender of pots and a seaman swap useful advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips exchanged' swaps the first and last letters of RASCAL. In Britain 'tinker' is an affectionate word for a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the word names a seaman from South Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: Old tanner from France in among teacher's mementos

indicators.note: among puts the three short pieces inside the word for the teacher's

parts.note: British pupils call a male teacher sir; with the possessive s it gives SIRS
UV, ultraviolet light, is what tans the skin
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A French sixpence turns up among a schoolmaster's keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was British slang for the old sixpence coin, but here it is what tans your skin. 'among' is the container signal, and 'from France' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: keepsakes kept to remember a place or event.

clue.text: Each going on with honeymoon, finally, in s American location

indicators.note: going on says the word for each is attached after the word for with

parts.note: and can mean with, as in bread and butter
EA is the abbreviation for each, as on price lists

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Two newlyweds are both carrying on with their honeymoon at last, somewhere in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for something found in the great mountain range running down that continent.

clue.text: Drink hosts dry in pursuit of a partner!

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the drink part follows behind the letter given by a
hosts says the drink has the word for dry as a guest inside it

parts.note: beer is a drink
TT, teetotal, describes someone who is dry, drinking no alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone throwing a drinks party stays sober while chasing a date.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags a partner in crime, not in romance. 'hosts' is the container signal and 'in pursuit of' only fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: one who aids and encourages a wrongdoer is an accomplice in the crime.

clue.text: As reported, mainly idle pupil of professor

indicators.note: as reported means the phrase is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: someone who is mainly idle will do little

explanation.surface: Word has it that the professor's student is lazy most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza, the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, is taught to speak by Professor Higgins.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary example: the surname of Eliza, whom Professor Higgins coaches in Pygmalion.

clue.text: Yours truly had turned up in gold and black, extremely late for hearing

indicators.note: in places the turned-round piece between the gold and the black

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: turned up reads the piece from bottom to top in a down entry

parts.note: yours truly is I, so yours truly had is I'd

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of the next word

explanation.surface: The writer arrived dressed in gold and black, very late for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearing is the sense, not a court session. 'turned up' gives DI, which 'in' sets between the two colours, and 'extremely' takes the outside of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a sound loud enough to be picked up by the ear.

clue.text: Some philanthropic backing for old ringmaster

indicators.note: backing says the letters found are read from right to left
some means only part of the long word is used

explanation.surface: A bit of charitable funding for a retired circus boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ILA from inside philanthropic and 'backing' turns it round. The ring is a boxing ring, not a circus one.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description of Muhammad, the former heavyweight champion who dominated boxing.

clue.text: Thus some footwear quotes read out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody recites the prices given for various shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' looks like a soundalike signal, but only 'out' is the indicator and 'read' is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes shoes or boots made with a blunt, boxy front.

clue.text: Was in red to welcome girl, lost in admiration

indicators.note: to welcome means the debt word takes the girl's name inside it

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt, so someone who was in the red owed
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in scarlet to greet a young woman is left speechless by her.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: so impressed by something as to be struck with wonder and silenced.

clue.text: Ill-fated lover, not that able to ignore the odds

parts.note: of the two demonstratives, the one that is not that is this

indicators.note: ignoring the odds drops the odd-numbered letters, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A doomed romantic is not really capable of disregarding how poor the chances are.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythological example: Pyramus's beloved, who killed herself after finding him dead.

clue.text: Start shunning either of two poets, and scoff

indicators.note: start shunning means the word avoids, and so loses, its opening letter

parts.note: Keats and Yeats differ only in their first letter, so either poet works

explanation.surface: Begin avoiding both of a pair of poets and mock them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start shunning' removes the first letter, and Keats or Yeats gives the same result. Scoff here is British slang for food, not mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal nouns: both are slang for food.

clue.text: Sent choir off to find hymn

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad or astray and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The singers are dispatched to hunt down a piece of sacred music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a short liturgical verse sung in Eastern Orthodox services.

clue.text: Hassle involving one great Britain runs as powerful spy

indicators.note: involving says the word for hassle wraps round the three short pieces

parts.note: bother is trouble or hassle
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Trouble surrounds a major agent whom Britain operates as a mighty spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Orwell's all-seeing ruler in Nineteen Eighty-Four. 'involving' is the container signal; 'runs' is a cricket abbreviation, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: Orwell's dictator who watches every citizen all the time.

clue.text: Something inspired primarily by wet weather, with hail

indicators.note: primarily asks for only the leading letter of the word after it

parts.note: rain is wet weather
to hail someone is to wave to them, as when hailing a taxi

explanation.surface: A creative idea was prompted mostly by a storm of rain and hailstones.
explanation.walkthrough: Hail is the verb, signalling to someone, not the icy weather the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden clever idea that arrives in a flash.

clue.text: Exploits poor eager Tess

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of unfortunate, keen Tess.
explanation.walkthrough: Exploits is a noun here, great deeds, not the verb of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning things done, used for a record of achievements or deeds.

clue.text: Eastern country cheers one chap protecting couple after I set about one

indicators.note: protecting says the thanks, the one and the chap together shelter the other group inside them

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you, as is cheers
I is the Roman numeral for one
Stan is a man's name

indicators.note: set about means the pair of letters is placed round the second one

parts.note: the two letters that follow I in the alphabet are J and K
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A country in the East applauds a man who shielded a pair after the speaker attacked somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple after I' is not two people but the alphabet's next two letters. 'set about' wraps them round the second 'one', making JIK, which 'protecting' then tucks inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Central Asian republic bordering Afghanistan and China.

clue.text: To show spirit, answer as quickly in French, briefly

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: briefly cuts the French word short by its last letter

parts.note: vite is the French word for quickly

explanation.surface: To prove you have pluck, reply just as fast in French, and keep it short.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Scandinavian liquor flavoured with caraway.

clue.text: Time for filling northern people's senses

indicators.note: for filling means the letter for time goes inside the people's name

parts.note: the Inuit are an Arctic people; with the possessive s it gives INUITS

explanation.surface: It is the moment to feed the faculties of those who live up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Senses is a verb here, perceives by instinct, not the five faculties.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: knows or perceives by instinct without reasoning.

clue.text: Spurs for one game, originally heading for Stoke

parts.note: for one means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: originally asks for the letter the next word begins with
the heading of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: Tottenham's footballers were travelling to a match in Stoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of the London football club Tottenham Hotspur, but here it is a verb meaning urges on.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: urges or goads someone on.

clue.text: Edinburgh's goes towards, mostly, music

indicators.note: mostly keeps all of the Scots phrase except its last letter

parts.note: in Scots, as spoken in Edinburgh, gangs means goes and tae means to or towards

explanation.surface: People in the Scottish capital mainly head for where the tunes are.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a style of rap about violent street life.

clue.text: Remain standing to drink, taking in flower of Scotland

indicators.note: taking in says the drinking word swallows the Scottish river

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a flower can be something that flows, and the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Fans stay on their feet with a pint while singing Scotland's anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower of Scotland is the Scottish sporting anthem, but the flower here is something that flows, a river. 'taking in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: to continue upright and not fall down.

clue.text: Braided uniform hasn't this? Probably not

indicators.note: braiding interweaves strands, so the letters are woven into a new order

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dress uniform trimmed with gold braid is unlikely to come with casual summer headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the answer, something a braided uniform probably lacks. 'Braided' rearranges U plus HASNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reference: the clue points at a piece of summer headgear a dress uniform would lack.

clue.text: Opinion linked to popular case

indicators.note: linked to joins the word for opinion onto the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or opinion taken on something

explanation.surface: Public feeling is tied to a much-followed court trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an example or occurrence, as in 'in this case'.

clue.text: Three couples marrying, madly worshipped mother

parts.note: three couples make six people, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: madly suggests the letters of the next word are thrown about wildly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Six people wed in a frenzy and adore the mother of one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious figure: the mother of Jesus, venerated by Christians.

clue.text: Hard class to prepare

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, firm or solidified, like concrete that has hardened
in British schools, a group of pupils of similar ability taught together
to make ready, as with laying a table or a trap

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: solidified, a school ability group, and to make ready.

clue.text: Feel like hugs: is making up!

indicators.note: hugs says the word for like wraps its arms round the word for feel

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
the feel of a place or piece of writing is its tone or atmosphere

explanation.surface: Somebody fancies a cuddle because a quarrel is being patched up.
explanation.walkthrough: Making up is making amends for a wrong, not reconciling after a row. 'Feel' is a noun, the mood of something, and 'hugs' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: makes amends, compensates for a fault.

clue.text: Record winning move after man finds a wife?

indicators.note: after says the record and the winning move come behind the word for man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
mate, short for checkmate, is the move that wins a game of chess

explanation.surface: After a personal best and a decisive chess victory, a fellow gets himself a bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Example, hence the question mark: a supportive companion, traditionally said of a spouse.
